text:
There are two Sharks teams this season. One is Macklin Celebrini between Will Smith and Igor Chernyshov, a line generating 4.58 expected goals per 60 minutes and winning 62% of the chances in its 64 minutes together. The other is everybody else, and it is why San Jose is 7-10-1 and winless in four, outscored 18-5 in that stretch.

That skid is not bad luck. The Sharks had 39% of the expected goals over those four games, and they are giving up 3.96 expected goals per 60 for the season, a number no defense survives for long. The penalty kill bleeds nearly a full expected goal a game. The second line of Kiefer Sherwood, Michael Misa and Ivar Stenberg is at 34% of the chances, a hard first stretch for two young centers. The Darnell Nurse and Michael Kesselring pair has been on for 10 goals against and three for.

Oddly, the record is a little kinder than the process: 15 points against about 14 deserved. And the goaltending has actually held up better than the shots, 64 goals allowed on 72.5 expected, which tells you how many good looks the defense is conceding.

Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest called the 4-1 loss in Minnesota "a better performance." That's the bar right now. Our simulations give them a 5% playoff chance, so the season is about Celebrini's line getting company.
headline: Celebrini's line works. Nothing else does yet
